newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hedge funds linked to unusual JGB options buying.
newsitem.headline: Hedge funds linked to unusual JGB options buying.

text.p: Overseas hedge funds may be behind the recent heavy buying of out-of-the-money Japanese government bond futures put options, traders said on Thursday.

"There is a rumour that hedge funds have bought about 6,000 lots of June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 123.00 since the start of the week," a senior trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
On Thursday, June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 122.00 were also heavily traded, and turnover amounted to 2,042 contracts.
Turnover of the 123.00 put option was 985 contracts on Thursday.
The 123.00 put option had the largest open interest out of all June JGB futures put options listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange -- 1.4196 trillion yen.

Traders said hedge funds may be buying based on a view that the Bank of Japan may change its current ultra-low interest rate policy before the put options expire on May 30. Most domestic participants expect no such decision by the BOJ before that time.
"Japanese traders believe that a fall in JGB futures to below 123.00 in the near-term is unthinkable," said Hidenobu Furuhashi, manager at Toyo Trust & Banking Co Ltd's trading department.

He said this belief would be shattered if the government happened to come to a decision in the near term to use more public funds to help solve the bad loan problems of Japan's financial institutions.

"I think the use of public funds in any form, would totally change the scenario. It will likely lead to a change in the (BOJ's) low interest rate policy, and there will no longer be any reason to continue buying bonds," Furuhashi said.
However, traders said they do not expect a government decision on the public funds issue any time soon.
They said the motive behind the heavy buying of JGB futures put options was not clear.
"I don't know why the put options are being bought," a senior trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
He said there was speculation that hedge funds were buying them using profits garnered from stock transactions, or that they were conducting some type of arbitrage trade.
"In any case, if May 30 comes and goes without anything happening, the put options will become worthless," he said.
The key June 10-year JGB futures ended Thursday's Tokyo trade at 126.62.
